answer: Sybil resistance requires every identity to solve a fresh VDF: each modular squaring uses the previous result, so GPUs cannot divide one chain into parallel tasks. An attacker can launch clones in parallel, but must complete a separate sequential chain for each, imposing real elapsed time and compute cost before they qualify. A beacon fixes the challenge; unlike the fable of effortless cloning, no terrace of extra hardware removes the per-identity delay.
